story_purpose: Show why a household starts by finding existing policies before discussing a new purchase.

production_strategy.future_trigger: Enable platform variants or controlled experiments only after publication capacity increases.

continuity_value.current_item_value: Show the first practical step for making scattered policy records visible.
continuity_value.future_value_promise: Continue using evidence-bound everyday cases to explain how families can check treatment, expenses and insurance decisions without starting from product promotion.
continuity_value.target_audience: Households that have insurance records but cannot yet explain what they own or how to use it.

protagonist.immediate_goal: work out what insurance the family already has

audience_bridge.shared_situation: Important documents are scattered across several family members and devices.

scene_anchor.observable_detail: The fictional family cannot produce one complete list of the policies already held.

inciting_incident.event: A fictional family asks whether it should add another policy but cannot list its existing coverage.

expectation_gap.actual_outcome: pause the comparison and inventory existing documents first

attempt_and_feedback.first_action: They begin by trying to compare another product.
attempt_and_feedback.expected_feedback: The comparison will immediately identify what to buy.
attempt_and_feedback.actual_feedback: The missing inventory makes a responsible comparison premature.

pressure.description: The family has incomplete records and does not know which person holds each document.

choice_under_pressure.cost_or_tradeoff: the purchase discussion is delayed while documents are collected

turning_points.event: They decide to stop comparing until the existing policies are listed.
The inventory reveals that several documents were held in different places.
turning_points.after_value: coverage gaps and overlaps can now be checked

climax.action_or_revelation: The decision shifts from buying first to understanding the current situation first.

resolution.new_state: The fictional household has a list that can support a later decision.
resolution.remaining_uncertainty: The example does not determine whether any new policy is suitable.

emotion_beats.eliciting_appraisal: The viewer recognizes the ordinary mess of scattered documents.
A previously vague situation becomes something the family can inspect.

emotional_design.aftertaste: Relief comes from clarity, not from a product promise.

explanation_bridge.main_claim: Before considering an additional policy, make the existing situation visible.
explanation_bridge.boundary: This fictional story illustrates a workflow and is not individual advice or proof that purchasing should be delayed.
